title: Give a planning-round budget stop its own budget-reserve outcome
summary: The reserve check already exists (budget_reserve and preflight in reading.rs, called at admission, in retry, and before each planner and critic call). The gap is acceptance (3): a job stopped by it before a planning round still closes as a planning-stage failure. I read the request as giving that stop a distinct budget-reserve outcome; jobs 20261028-081326-zzxg and 20261028-082151-67fa are the incidents it came from, and this change adds no code for their disk and resume work.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the no-model-call hold and the distinct outcome by running tests.
cargo fmt, clippy and test are acceptance criteria.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (budget_reserve, ReserveStage, BudgetShort, Athena::preflight, Athena::retry), crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs (stop_planning, plan_round preflight calls at the planner and critic) and crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (preflight at Dispatch and Run). Admission uses Config::budget_required in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs. The entry points are admission, Athena::retry, dispatch, then plan_round. Existing tests: reading.rs shipped_budget_covers_the_reserve, run/tests.rs lines 1658 and 1709, run_pin_tests.rs line 994.

Existing code: this extends crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs and crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs (PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX). The reserve sum is not rebuilt; the check already compares the remaining budget with the producer, verifier and next planner caps.

Job 20261028-081326-zzxg (disk and resume work) and job 20261028-082151-67fa (retry that stopped on budget) produced no candidate. Their findings concern disk cleanup and resuming from a kept candidate, which this request does not ask for, so they do not apply; the changed-file set of both is empty, so no earlier work is kept or dropped.

Today the planning-round stop calls stop_planning, which closes the job with PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX, the planning-stage failure the request wants distinguished. I assume a new prefix constant for the budget-reserve outcome, which retry_findings and introspection treat as an environment-like hold and not as a failure of the work.
Budget amounts in athena.toml stay unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a test with $5.48 left and a $5.75 reserve before a planning round makes no planner call and closes with a message naming the remaining budget, the reserve and the shortfall ($0.27).
Run cargo test -p athena-core: a test with enough budget shows the planner is invoked and planning goes ahead.

Run cargo test -p athena-core: a job that cannot afford another planning round ends with a distinct budget-reserve outcome. Its reason does not start with PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX, and the test asserts that.
Grep of crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs shows the preflight failure path uses the new budget-reserve stop and no longer calls stop_planning with the planning-stage prefix.
Run cargo test -p athena-core: retry and admission checks still refuse a short budget before any model call (existing run_pin_tests.rs and reading.rs tests pass).
git diff shows no change to athena.toml, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the new budget-reserve outcome.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test pass, with no unrelated behavior changes.

out_of_scope: Changing the 10 GB free-disk minimum, disk cleanup before the verifier, or resume from a kept candidate (jobs 20261028-081326-zzxg and 20261028-082151-67fa)
Adding a partial-plan resume for the planner
departures: The reserve check already exists, so the work is narrow, but the reading may be refused if this view of the gap is wrong. The request names only reading.rs while the change likely touches planning.rs and records.
hard_reason: The job changes a rule that holds or refuses work (the budget reserve) and how a job closes in the run pipeline.
